about.title: Cudahy Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Cudahy is a small, densely packed city, and its main streets carry a lot of daily traffic through tight intersections and residential blocks. Public records show 34 injury collisions and 51 people injured here in the most recent reporting year, with Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m. showing up often in the count. Corridors like Atlantic Avenue, Wilcox Avenue, Clara Street, and Santa Ana Street see a good share of that activity simply because of how much traffic moves through them. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the days right after matter: insurance adjusters move quickly, and evidence like skid marks, vehicle damage, and witness memory fades fast. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we're a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options under California law, without any upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government vehicle or road defect was involved. An attorney can flag early which deadline applies to your case.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Affect Your Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly blamed for the crash, though your share of fault reduces the amount. Insurers know this and often push blame onto injured drivers early — an attorney can help push back with facts.

items.title: No Cap Means Your Story Matters
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a car accident case, so documenting how the injury has actually affected your life is worth doing carefully. An attorney can help make sure that part of your claim isn't shortchanged.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: I was hurt near the Atlantic Avenue and Clara Street area in Cudahy — does location affect my claim?
items.answer: Where the crash happened can matter for evidence purposes, like nearby traffic cameras, businesses with surveillance footage, or witnesses. It doesn't change your legal rights, but documenting the specific location and time helps build a clearer picture of what happened. An attorney can help gather that evidence before it disappears.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after an initial conversation.
